test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - Numerical Ability (Held on: 20 Nov, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: Two stations, A and B are 100 km apart on a straight line. One train starts from A at 7 A.M. and travels towards B at a speed of 20 km/h. Another train starts from B at 8 A.M. and travels towards A at a speed of 25 km/h. At what time they will meet?
solution:
**Given:**

Distance between A and B = 100 km

Speed of Train A = 20 km/h

Speed of Train B = 25 km/h

Train A starts at 7 A.M.

Train B starts at 8 A.M.

**Formula used:**

Relative speed when two trains are moving towards each other = Speed of Train A + Speed of Train B

Time taken to meet = Distance / Relative Speed

**Calculation:**

Relative speed = 20 km/h + 25 km/h = 45 km/h

Train A travels 1 hour before Train B starts, so distance covered by Train A in 1 hour = 20 km

Remaining distance = 100 km - 20 km = 80 km

Time taken to cover remaining distance at relative speed = 80 km / 45 km/h

⇒ Time = 80 / 45 hours

⇒ Time = 1.78 hours

Convert 1.78 hours into hours and minutes:

1.78 hours = 1 hour + (0.78 × 60) minutes ≈ 1 hour 47 minutes

⇒ Time ≈ 1 hour 47 minutes

Train B starts at 8 A.M., so they will meet at 8 A.M. + 1 hour 47 minutes

⇒ Meeting time = 9:47 A.M.

**∴ The correct answer is option 4.**
